newsitem.title: USA: Lands' End profits rise 45 percent in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Lands' End profits rise 45 percent in quarter.

text.p: Mail order clothing retailer Lands' End Inc. said Thursday its earnings rose 45 percent in its fiscal fourth quarter amid healthy growth in sales per page from its catalogue operations.

"Our speciality, new and international businesses all grew strongly during the year," Chief Executive Officer Michael Smith said in a statement. "Most important, we've seen a turnaround in productivity, or sales per page, in our core monthly and prospecting catalogues."

Dodgeville, Wis.-based Lands' End said its earnings rose to $37.4 million, or $1.15 a share, for the fourth quarter ended Jan. 31, from $25.8 million, or 77 cents, a year ago, which included a $1.9 million charge for the sale of a subsidiary. Excluding the charge, the year-ago fourth-quarter income was $26.9 million, or 80 cents a share.
Sales rose to $423 million from $399 million.

Lands' End also said its year-end inventory dropped 14 percent to $142 million from $165 million a year earlier as sales improved in the last part of the fiscal third quarter. This cut into the company's holiday season inventory and increased the number of lost sales and raised the percentage of items it was forced to ship on back-order.

"Sales began to improve strongly in the last part of the third quarter," Smith said. "Because of this, we began the holiday season with lower than optimal inventory and were unable to fill orders at our usual seasonal rate in the fourth quarter.
"For the year, we shipped 86 percent of items ordered at the time the order was placed, compared with 90 percent in the prior year," Smith said.
For the full fiscal year, the company earned $50.9 million, or $1.54 a share, vs. $30.6 million, or 89 cents a share, a year ago. Sales rose to $1.12 biillion from $1.03 billion.
Lands' End stock was 87.5 cents higher at $29 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
